name: Lying Leg Curl
grip: Hands gripping side support handles on the machine bench.
description: Flex knees against a padded machine roller while lying prone on an angled bench, isolating the hamstring complex through open-chain knee flexion.
setup: Select the desired pin load on the weight stack.
Adjust the padded roller so it rests just below the calves against the lower Achilles tendon with knees aligned with the machine pivot axis.
Lie prone with your hips and torso supported against the angled bench pads and grasp the side handles firmly.
instructions: Curl both heels upward and backward toward your glutes by flexing your knees through a smooth, controlled arc.
Keep your hips and pelvis pressed firmly against the bench pad without hyperextending your lower back.
Squeeze your hamstrings firmly at peak contraction when the roller approaches the glutes.
Lower the lever slowly under control back to the starting position with legs nearly fully extended before the next rep.
cues: Glue your hips to the bench.
Pull heels all the way to the glutes.
commonMistakes: Lifting the pelvis and hips off the bench pad to recruit hip flexors and lower back.
Using explosive swinging momentum that slams the weight stack at the bottom.
Setting the roller pad too high on the calf or too low on the foot.

logging.example: Weight stack pin set to 35 kg: record 35 kg selected machine load.
logging.note: Cam shapes and lever ratios vary across machine manufacturers; record the selected stack pin load.

variantNote: Prone selectorized lying leg curl machine isolating knee flexion. Angled bench pad reduces passive insufficiency by placing hips in slight flexion.
